quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road or pavement edge, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and gradually steer back onto the road when it is safe.
Turn back onto the road immediately.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and gradually steer back onto the road when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the road right away. Reduce your speed, look for traffic, and then gradually steer back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: You are entering a crowded freeway. What should you do to merge safely?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Speed up on the entrance ramp to match the freeway traffic speed.
Let traffic already on the freeway go first.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to reach the same speed as freeway traffic. Yield to cars already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure it is safe to merge.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane next to the solid yellow line.
No one can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross it. So you can only pass from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle on your right, you must yield to that vehicle. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What color are temporary signs in construction and work zones?

options.text: Red background with green writing.
Orange background with black writing.
Yellow background with blue writing.

questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign that has no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After making a complete stop and confirming it is safe to proceed.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing down to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After making a complete stop and confirming it is safe to proceed.
questions.explanation: You must make a complete stop at a stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: It warns you about road or traffic conditions ahead.
It helps you find cities and towns.
It tells you about traffic laws.
It tells you about road construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns you about road or traffic conditions ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs with a yellow background and black symbols warn you about conditions on or near the road.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?

options.text: Excessive braking.
Sudden stops.
Sudden turns.
Driving too fast.

questions.explanation: When you drive too fast, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose grip and the vehicle slides on water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: A driver turning left must yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Always yield to oncoming traffic and bicycles when making a left turn. You can complete the turn when the way is clear.

questions.question: By driving on South Carolina roads, you agree to take a chemical test if a police officer asks.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: South Carolina has an implied consent law. By driving in the state, you agree to take a chemical test for intoxication if a police officer requests it.

questions.question: When approaching an accident scene, what should you do?

options.text: Focus on your own driving.
Keep driving.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived yet. Focus on your driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to accident scenes, fires, or disasters just to look.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Drive through because drivers always have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Turn right and pass behind the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: At a crosswalk, you must yield to all pedestrians. Continue driving only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street the wrong way.
School crossing ahead.
Do not use this lane.
Cars turning left on green must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars turning left on green must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign is used with a traffic light to warn drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way. Wait for oncoming traffic to pass before turning.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive no faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: You must use your headlights when you can only see 500 feet ahead. Use low beams in fog or rain. High beams will reflect back into your eyes and reduce visibility.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level above the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving ability suffers. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: Can you park in the access aisles next to handicap parking spaces?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: No one can park in handicap access aisles. These spaces are needed for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: What colors are used on warning signs for upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on white background
Black letters or symbols on yellow background
White letters or symbols on blue background
White letters or symbols on green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs for hazards are yellow with black letters or symbols. Construction zone warning signs are orange with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: When must you use your headlights?

options.text: After 6 p.m. and before 7 a.m.
After 7 p.m. and before 8 a.m.
After 8 p.m. and before 7 a.m. during daylight savings time.
From sunset to sunrise.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights from one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise. Also use them when visibility is low.

questions.question: What should you do to make sure your physical condition does not cause unsafe driving?

options.text: Stay physically fit and have regular checkups.
Know how medicine affects your driving.
Drive within your physical limits.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Your physical health affects your ability to drive safely. Know your limits and drive only when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Stay farther back than usual.

questions.explanation: When following a motorcycle, keep a distance of at least 3 to 4 seconds behind it. Motorcycles can stop quickly. Staying too close puts both of you at risk. If the rider falls, you need extra space to avoid them. Falls are most likely on wet or icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges or train tracks.

questions.question: What should you do when someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is available, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear. This encourages the tailgater to pass you.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: If someone tailgates you and a right lane is open, move to it. If no right lane exists, slow down gradually when the road is clear ahead. This encourages the tailgater to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.
Busy sidewalk.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a pedestrian crossing. Watch for people crossing the road. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Drivers do not have to yield to pedestrians who cross against the traffic light.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You should always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are breaking the law. Yield to pedestrians, vehicles, bicyclists, and anyone else already in the intersection before you enter it.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights ahead. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down. Change lanes if possible so you do not drive beside the emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to quickly pass the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. Change lanes if possible so you do not drive beside the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must change lanes if safe to do so. If changing lanes is not possible, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much space as possible.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while talking to them during driving.
Only watches the car directly in front of them.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not look at passengers, search for objects in your car, read while driving, sightsee, or daydream. Keep scanning the road, checking mirrors, and looking at the instrument panel regularly. These safe habits help you stay focused.

questions.question: It is illegal to drive in the same lane as a motorcycle.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Never share a lane with a motorcycle. Even if there appears to be enough space, motorcyclists need the full lane width to maneuver safely.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: Blind spots around a truck or bus where vehicles cannot be seen.
A special speed zone.
A road with limits on stereo volume.
A television show.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind spots around a truck or bus where vehicles cannot be seen.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, behind, and in front. Cars in these areas cannot be seen. These areas are called the "No zone."

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Getting ahead of bad drivers in traffic to defend yourself.
Following the car in front of you at a close distance.
Quickly changing lanes and moving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means recognizing dangerous situations and taking action before an accident happens. It helps you avoid problems with reckless, careless, or dangerous drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: When a school bus stops on the road to load or unload children, what must you do?

options.text: Stop completely until all children have left the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes down.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes down.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm out, you must stop. Do not move until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Even after the bus moves, do not go forward until you are sure no children are crossing.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may not pass.
You may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means vehicles in both directions can pass. Only pass if it is safe and you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.
